events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
An active monsoon pattern will continue to bring scattered to
numerous, locally heavy, showers and isolated to scattered
thunderstorms across portions of Yap State through Thursday night.
Frequent lightning, wind gusts to 25 knots, and choppy seas can be
expected with thunderstorms. Inter-island travel will be hazardous
through at least this Thursday night. Several inches of rain have
already fallen with this event, which is on top of the foot of rain
Yap saw last week. Due to saturated conditions, flash flooding and
mudslides are expected where the heaviest rain occurs. Residents
across Yap State should monitor local forecasts and heed advice of
emergency managers when heavy rainfall occurs.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Elevated surf of 4-6 feet with sets to 7 feet expected
along with dangerous rip currents and minor coastal flooding.

* WHERE...San Diego County coastal areas and Orange County
coastal areas, particularly along south and southwest-facing
beaches.

* WHEN...From early Wednesday morning through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Flooding of low lying beach parking
lots, boardwalks, and roads.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides peak around 6.2 to 6.5 feet
from 8-10 PM PDT on Wednesday and Thursday.
